C5M.1: Make a bass bite on demand, opening the filter and sharpening its edge together from a named knob you can grab mid-phrase.
C5M.2: Fade between layers of a sound with a single turn, such as a buzzy bass giving way to a hollow tone across a phrase.
C5M.3: Automate a single knob through a build and the whole instrument seems to brighten naturally, instead of sounding like a filter being turned.
C5M.4: Widen a pad or lead for the big section of a track without it jumping out of the mix, since the level eases back as it spreads.
C5M.5: Ride a still bass into a deeper, faster wobble during a build, all from a control you can turn as the tension rises.
C5M.6: The same sound can play short plucked notes in a verse and long swelling chords in a breakdown, with a single knob travelling between them.
C5M.7: Take a clean bass from polite to filthy by degrees, and stop at exactly the amount of grit the section calls for.
C5M.8: With brightness and wobble on separate knobs, you can perform a bass part by hand and find a different sound at every combination.
C5M.9: Push a sound from right in front of you to the back of a hall, handy for breakdowns where a lead should drift away.
C5M.10: Flick a knob on the last note of a phrase and it echoes off into the gap, while the rest of the part stays clean.
C5M.11: Drive a bass hard for warmth and weight while its top end stays smooth, so heavy distortion does not turn fizzy in the mix.
C5M.12: That tearing, rising sweep becomes something you play by hand, dark at the bottom and bright only as it reaches the top.
C5M.13: Turn a plain low sine into a snarling, fast-moving growl whenever the drop needs it, and ease it back just as easily.
C5M.14: Even out soft and hard notes in a bassline as much as the part needs, without the whole sound getting quieter as you squeeze.
C5M.15: Open a plain pad or pluck into something wide, drifting and airy for a lift, with a move gentle enough to use fully.
C5M.16: Dial a kick from a soft round thud to a hard bright hit that still comes through on small speakers, to suit each track.
C5M.C: Returning to a sound you liked gets easier when your ears can judge how far a knob that changes several things was turned.
